ashley (support): Hey team — customer CoreStream hit repeated 429s this morning during a short promotional burst. They say it was ~3 minutes long and suddenly spiked from 50 req/s to ~1200 req/s. They want to understand burst credits and smoothing behavior. Any pointers before I reply?

mike (sre): ugh, yep that pattern rings a bell. Do we have the request-id(s) from their logs? Need to confirm whether they hit per-account token quota or platform-wide rate limiter.

ashley (support): I asked for request-ids, they sent one: rcpt-9b2f3a. They also pasted the response headers from our API showing: `x-rw-retry-after: 10` and `x-rw-burst-remaining: 0`.

jamie (engineer): nice, those headers are useful. `x-rw-burst-remaining: 0` means they exhausted their transient burst credits for that account/pool. The flow: each account has a steady-state quota and a small burst bucket that refills slowly. Burst credits let short spikes pass without immediate 429s up to a cap.

ashley (support): how small is "small"? Customer is upset because this was a 2–3 minute marketing push.

jamie (engineer): it depends on plan + routing. For hosted standard tier the typical burst window is ~60–90s of extra capacity above baseline, then the bucket depletes. We cap single-request concurrency and per-minute tokens too. If they sustained 1200 req/s for 3 minutes they'll likely exhaust credits.

mike (sre): also important: when the runtime sees sudden connection bursts it triggers smoothing to prevent downstream overload. That means we intentionally throttle new requests to keep latency SLOs for others. So clients might see rapid 429s early in the spike even if averaged throughput later would be fine.

ashley (support): customer asked if they were billed for the requests that 429'd. They looked charged for succeeded requests but worried about quota impact.

lina (billing): we don't bill for requests that return 429 — only successful calls and charged units. But the throttling still consumes bursts; the bucket was drained by accepted calls and by the smoothing algorithm's "reservation" behavior. I'll confirm exact invoice lines if they share account id.

ashley (support): they gave account id corestream-42. Could you check billing?

lina (billing): noted. I'll look after we confirm which requests succeeded.

jamie (engineer): for the reply to the customer I'd suggest: explain how burst credits work, point to tunables, and offer mitigation patterns: client-side jittered exponential backoff, token-bucket pacing, and pre-warming via a short ramp-up before the promo peak. Also offer Dedicated if they expect repeated sustained spikes.

ashley (support): can you give a short bullet list I can paste?

jamie (engineer): sure — paste this: 
- We provide a small per-account burst bucket that absorbs short spikes but refills slowly (order of minutes).
- Sustained high-rate spikes (> baseline for multiple minutes) will exhaust burst credits and trigger 429s.
- Our smoothing layer may proactively throttle new connections during abrupt surges to maintain latency SLOs for other customers.
- Mitigations: client-side exponential backoff with jitter, rate-limited queueing on the client, warm-up ramp (gradual increase over 60–90s), or request Dedicated capacity for predictable bursty traffic.

mike (sre): add this operational note: if you see `x-rw-burst-remaining: 0` combined with `x-rw-retry-after`, it's safe to recommend backoff per that Retry-After header; if they repeatedly hit 429s despite backoff we can whitelist short-term increases or advise a temporary quota bump.

ashley (support): they asked for repro steps so they can run a test and validate. Any safe test we can suggest that won't affect other customers?

jamie (engineer): recommend a staged load test using a single API key from their staging account. Example curl loop we can give them (use small concurrent workers and ramp slowly):

# naive example (do not start at full ramp)
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.2
done
wait

Explain: start with sleep 0.2 then reduce to 0.05 etc. Watch `x-rw-burst-remaining` header.

ashley (support): good. Anything to add about logs or headers we should collect?

mike (sre): yes — ask them to capture: request-id, `x-rw-burst-remaining`, `x-rw-retry-after`, response code, and timestamp. Also client-side timing (latency). If they can provide a short pcap or HAR that's helpful.

ashley (support): customer says they saw `x-rw-burst-remaining: 0` but `x-rw-retry-after` varied between 5 and 15. Should we expect variation?

jamie (engineer): the Retry-After is computed by the rate limiter based on current queue depth and per-route smoothing state. So yes it can vary quickly as load changes. Treat it as a signal to back off and reattempt after that window.

ops-bot: Deploy completed: rollout/rate-limiter-tweak v2.1 applied to prod cluster us-east-1 at 2026-03-15T09:42:00Z :rocket:

mike (sre): FYI we just rolled a small change to make the smoothing decay a bit more permissive for short bursts (experimental). That may reduce 429s for promos that are <90s, but not a guarantee.

ashley (support): perfect. I'll tell the customer: (1) why it happened; (2) what to capture for repro; (3) mitigation steps; (4) offer temporary quota bump or Dedicated consult. Any wording tweaks?

jamie (engineer): emphasize the safe test on staging and suggest they run a quick ramp with monitoring. Offer to open a support ticket where we can monitor the keys in real-time near the next promo.

lina (billing): I'll standby on billing — if they want a temporary quota bump we'll need a signed addendum for usage-based increases for that billing cycle.

ashley (support): Thanks everyone — sending reply now and offering an ops-coordinated test next week. :thumbsup:

mike (sre): thx. If they do the test ping me in #eng-sre and include the request-ids. We'll tail the runtime logs and confirm whether smoothing or strict quota fired.

ashley (support): will do. Closing this thread for now but will reopen if they run tests.
